title: Spring
summary: Spring was a season of renewal and movement. As the weather warmed, families could shift from more protected winter places toward fields, streams, bays, and other seasonal work areas. Spring fish runs brought alewives, shad, striped bass, and other fish into freshwater streams, while early plant foods and new growth marked changes in the year.
content:
Planting required close attention to the land, sky, and water. Project sources describe signs such as fish moving upstream, dogwood leaves opening, and seasonal stars changing position as part of planting-time knowledge. Corn, beans, and squash were planted in mounds, while shell or bone tools could be used to prepare the soil.

Spring also connects to community renewal. June Meeting, remembered and continued in Shinnecock and Unkechaug community life, shows that seasonal gatherings are not only part of the past. They remain tied to kinship, worship, memory, and Native continuity.
